title: S&P Select Sector Indices December rebalance — reference close (sets the capped weights the 12-30 secondary test drifts from)
source: EST: date derived by applying an SEC-filed rule to the 2026 calendar. The rule is quoted verbatim from SEC EDGAR, Select Sector SPDR Trust Form 497 (accession 0001193125-26-031948, document d85739d497.htm), fetched direct 2026-09-08 by this proposer (HTTP 200, 2,388,335 bytes): 'The rebalancing of the Select Sector Indices, based on the processes described above, occurs at the closing prices of the second Friday of March, June, September and December. Changes will become effective after the market close on the third Friday of March, June, September and December.' The second Friday of December 2026 is 2026-12-11 and the third Friday is 2026-12-18 (weekday arithmetic computed mechanically by this session). Filed estimate rather than SEC:/confirmed on the same two counts the identical 2027 entry recorded: the filing dates the RULE, not this instance — no 2026-dated S&P DJI or SPDR announcement of the December reference close was fetched — and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2026-12-31 initial research (2026-09-08), which found it by enumerating its own reset-to-test window rather than by reading a new source. THIS IS A GAP IN THE MIDDLE OF AN ALREADY-TRACKED SEQUENCE, which is the whole reason it is worth filing: the calendar carries the September 2026 pair (sp-rebalance-proforma-2026-09-04, sp-rebalance-proforma-capped-2026-09-11) and the March 2027 entry (sp-rebalance-reference-close-2027-03-12, whose own notes describe itself as following that September pair) — and carries NOTHING for December 2026, the quarter between them. WHY IT IS LOAD-BEARING FOR THE PROPOSER: this close is the input that sets the capped index weights the 2026-12-30 secondary breach test measures drift from. Under the filing's step 1 a name over 24% is reduced to 23.00%, and the proposer's whole refusal is priced off the +4.35% relative move needed to get back over 24.00% from there in the seven sessions to 12-30. If this close does not strike on schedule, that arithmetic has no anchor. TWO THINGS THE RESEARCHING LANE SHOULD ESTABLISH, because this proposal deliberately did not: (1) whether S&P DJI publishes a December pro-forma-file release date distinct from the reference close — the September pair is titled for pro-forma files and the March 2027 entry deliberately is not, because the 497 is primary evidence for the reference close and the effective date and evidence for neither pro-forma release date; (2) the same session carries russell-reconstitution-2026-12-11, FTSE Russell's first-ever December semi-annual reconstitution (medium impact) — two index families striking reference/recon business on one close is a corridor fact worth sizing, and neither this proposal nor the proposer priced it. Low impact and market-structure only: it changes execution timing, never direction, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4/G1) is index-flow-keyed. Kind sector matches every sibling in the sequence.
